title: Onias and the Oniad High Priests
lead: The Oniads were the priestly family that held the high priesthood in Jerusalem for much of the Greek period. They included Onias I, Simon I, Onias II, Simon II (praised in Sirach 50) and Onias III. 2 Maccabees makes Onias III the model of a godly high priest (3:1; 15:12), tells how his brother Jason bought the office and how he was murdered (4:7–34), and Josephus says a son of Onias founded a rival temple at Leontopolis in Egypt, which stood until AD 73.
